svg.title: Six-Layer Human Neocortical Laminar Architecture
svg.desc: Verified anatomical diagram of human neocortical layers I through VI showing cell types, primary afferent inputs, efferent projection targets, and major regional variations across sensory and motor cortex.
svg.text: Canonical laminar organization (~2–4 mm thick, ~16 billion cortical neurons) from pial surface to subcortical white matter
PIAL SURFACE (Cerebrospinal Fluid / Subarachnoid Space Above)
Cell-sparse synaptic zone; apical dendritic tufts of pyramidal cells, horizontal axons, and Cajal–Retzius / neurogliaform GABAergic interneurons.
Densely packed small pyramidal neurons and stellate interneurons mediating local intracortical processing and ipsilateral association connections.
Medium-to-large pyramidal neurons; principal source of long-range corticocortical association fibers and commissural projections across the corpus callosum.
Internal Granular Layer — Primary Thalamic Input Zone
Spiny stellate cells receiving specific thalamocortical sensory input (LGN → V1, VPL/VPM → S1, MGN → A1). Prominent in primary sensory cortex
(containing the white Stria of Gennari in V1); virtually absent in primary motor cortex (BA 4, termed "agranular cortex").
Internal Pyramidal (Ganglionic) Layer — Subcortical & Motor Output
Largest pyramidal neurons in the brain (including giant Betz cells in BA 4). Sends major subcortical outputs to basal ganglia (striatum), brainstem
nuclei, superior colliculus, and spinal cord via the corticospinal (pyramidal) tract.
Spindle-shaped fusiform and modified pyramidal cells projecting excitatory feedback back to the thalamus (and claustrum), closing thalamocortical loops.
SUBCORTICAL WHITE MATTER (Myelinated Association, Commissural & Projection Axons)
